From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Positions

I've reviewed the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003) against the buyer baseline: 100% of Paperbark Analytics, AUD 24m price, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law. I haven't seen the full SPA draft, so clause references follow the Seller's summary and need checking against the actual text. The Seller's figures are also as at 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026, so the record is about six weeks old. Before relying on any of this, have NSW-admitted transaction counsel check the statutory points.

## Core structural problem

Most of the known problems are disclosed against the warranties through the general disclosure in Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2. A disclosed matter generally can't ground a warranty claim. The buyer therefore can't rely on warranty recovery for Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses, the data incident or the supplier renewals. These must be handled through the price mechanism, conditions precedent and specific indemnities, not general warranties. Much of the Seller's package is designed to push known risk onto the buyer while limiting the buyer's recourse for unknown risk.

Known quantified items total roughly **AUD 4.13m** before on-costs and before any Bluefen revenue loss:

| Item | Amount | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~3.20m | DD-003 |
| Employee Completion bonuses | 0.42m (plus on-costs) | DD-005 |
| Sandbar supplier renewals | 0.33m | DD-008/DD-011 |
| Ironquay SOW3 open fees | 0.18m | DD-010 |

Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%), which implies total revenue near AUD 12m. A large share of the AUD 24m price therefore depends on a consent the Seller has not delivered.

## Issues and pushback

**1. General liability cap (cl. 12.1): 20% (AUD 4.8m).**
Capping general warranty exposure at a fifth of the price is well below market for a business of this kind. Push for a cap of at least 100% of price for fundamental and tax warranties, and a general cap of at least 30–50%, with the Seller's exposure matched to what the buyer is paying.

**2. Thresholds (cl. 12.2): AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k excess-only basket.**
A deductible basket means the first AUD 250k is absorbed by the buyer, and recovery is limited to the excess. Push for:
- a tipping basket (once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar), or a smaller deductible;
- a lower de minimis, with related claims aggregated so they can't be split below the threshold;
- the basket and de minimis not to apply to fundamental, tax, or specific-indemnity claims.

**3. Time limits (cl. 12.3 / 13): 18 months for general warranties; "any limitation applies to all Claims."**
Eighteen months is too short for a business with tax, IP and privacy exposure. Under the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW), contract claims generally run for six years, and the ATO's amendment period for income tax is generally four years from lodgement, so tax claims can surface well after 18 months. Push for:
- general warranties: 24–36 months;
- fundamental and title warranties: six years or the statutory limit;
- tax claims: 60 days after the statute of limitations expires;
- rejection of the blanket "any limitation applies to all Claims" wording. Each class needs its own period.

**4. Fundamental/title warranties subject to general caps and time limits.**
Title and capacity are the core of what the buyer is paying for. Reject this outright. Title and capacity should sit outside the general cap, with a cap of at least the price and an extended time limit. The title position also relies on the DD-012 share register alone (see issue 13).

**5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).**
This wording would reach fraud and possibly statutory misleading-conduct claims. Push for:
- express carve-outs for fraud, fundamental warranties, tax indemnity, specific indemnities and wilful default;
- a clause confirming nothing excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded under Australian consumer or corporations law (verify the exact statutory carve-outs with counsel);
- non-reliance limited to extra-contractual representations, not the SPA warranties themselves.

**6. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Schedule 7; DL §1.1–1.2).**
"Every fact... contained or referred to in" the data room is a blanket disclosure of the entire record. It would disclose matters the buyer never read and turns the warranties into a dead letter. Push for:
- disclosure only against specific warranties, with reasonable particularity;
- no general data room disclosure; a disclosed document is only disclosed to the extent it is fairly disclosed on its face;
- deletion of §1.2 or limitation to specifically identified registers.

**7. Buyer knowledge / anti-sandbagging (cl. 8.3).**
This would bar claims for anything the buyer or its advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records. Given the disclosure record, this clause would strip most of the buyer's protection. Push for:
- deletion, and an express pro-sandbagging clause so the buyer's knowledge does not limit warranty claims (Australian law on this point isn't fully settled, so express drafting matters);
- for known issues, specific indemnities or price adjustments, since the buyer knows about them and needs protection that doesn't depend on the warranties.

**8. Bluefen change-control consent (cl. 3 / 6.3; DL §2).**
The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and deems consent satisfied on delivery of written consent. The disclosure confirms there is no final written consent and the conditions in cl. 11.3 are unmet. Bluefen is about 30% of revenue. Push for:
- consent as a hard condition precedent, not a reasonable-endeavours obligation;
- consent in agreed form, unconditional or on conditions acceptable to the buyer, with the cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied;
- if Bluefen is not delivered, a right to walk away, or a price reduction or escrow sized to the revenue at risk. Consider an earn-out-style deferral tied to Bluefen revenue continuing post-completion.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl. 2 / 7; DL §3).**
This is a debt-free/cash-free deal, so the AUD 3.2m must be paid off from the price at completion, not after it. The Seller's "release following Completion" leaves the buyer owning a company still encumbered by the lender's security. Push for:
- a payoff letter, repayment from the price at completion, and release of all security (including PPSR registrations and any guarantees) as a completion deliverable;
- the debt deducted from the price as a debt item;
- the change-of-control consent under DD-003 cl. 8.1 obtained before completion.

**10. Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1; DL §4).**
The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment, and ownership of SOW3 project materials transfers only on payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 records AUD 180k open, with no receipt or confirmatory assignment. Push for:
- the Seller to pay all outstanding Ironquay fees before completion, or the AUD 180k treated as a debt-like deduction from price;
- an unconditional confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a condition precedent;
- a specific indemnity covering all Ironquay claims, not just SOW3, with no cap below the price and a long time limit;
- IP warranties extended beyond the general regime.

**11. Employee bonuses (DL §5).**
AUD 420k of Completion bonuses is missing from the funds flow. The disclosure also doesn't say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply. In NSW, payroll tax and the 12% superannuation guarantee could add materially to that figure (verify current rates). Push for:
- bonuses, all on-costs and any related employment taxes treated as seller-borne transaction costs or debt-like items, deducted from the price;
- a specific indemnity for any employment-related liability arising from the bonuses or Completion-related payments;
- the funds flow corrected before signing.

**12. Export/privacy incident (cl. 4.6 / Sch. 6; DL §6).**
Calling this "preliminary and not expected to be material" is not acceptable. The file may hold about 1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps. The Seller admits it cannot establish whether anyone accessed it or whether notification is required. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), an eligible data breach requires assessment within 30 days. Given the September date, that window may already have passed. This needs urgent verification. Push for:
- a completed forensic and legal assessment before signing, including whether any notification was required and whether it was made;
- a specific indemnity, uncapped or subject to a high cap, for all costs, regulatory action, claims and notification costs, not dependent on a breach warranty (the Seller has disclaimed that the matter is a breach);
- a retention or escrow from the price until the matter is resolved;
- a warranty on data security and no unreported incidents, with a long time limit.

**13. Title (DL §10; DD-012).**
The share register is the source of title, but it doesn't confirm the buyer's own verification. Push for:
- a current ASIC company extract and independent verification of the share register;
- PPSR and other encumbrance searches over the shares and company assets;
- confirmation that no options, convertibles or other rights to shares exist;
- the title warranty outside the cap (issue 4), plus delivery of share transfers and certificates at completion.

**14. Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."**
Reject. Tax needs a standalone pre-completion tax indemnity, outside the cap and basket, with a time limit tied to the statute of limitations. IP warranties need their own treatment (issue 10).

**15. Office lease (cl. 7; DL §7).**
The Seller concedes a notification obligation but doesn't confirm whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale. Push for a confirmation from the landlord, or a landlord consent condition, and a review of the lease's change-of-control clause.

**16. Supplier renewals (DL §8; DD-008/DD-011).**
Three renewals of AUD 110k each, totalling AUD 330k, are described as ordinary course. Reading them together, they may be one commitment split into three. Push for:
- confirmation of whether they are committed pre-completion, whether they are terminable, and whether any prepaid amounts are involved;
- a buyer consent right over any Seller-agreed commitments outside the ordinary course before completion (interim operating covenant);
- any unavoidable or accrued cost treated as a debt-like item.

**17. Mossvale assignment restriction (DL §9).**
Push for a written confirmation that no consent is required for a share sale, or consent as a condition precedent if it is.

**18. Disclosure Letter §1.4 non-admission.**
This is standard and acceptable on its own, but it should not be read to limit the buyer's rights under the specific indemnities and price adjustments above.

**19. Currency of the record.**
The disclosure is as at 22 September 2026. Require a bring-down disclosure and an updated data room index before signing, and a bring-down of the warranties at completion.

## Summary of recommendations

**Priority 1: Must resolve before signing**
1. Bluefen consent as a hard condition precedent, or a price or escrow mechanism sized to the revenue at risk.
2. Riverlark repaid from the price at completion, with all security released as a completion deliverable.
3. Ironquay: fees paid, or the AUD 180k deducted; unconditional confirmatory IP assignment as a condition precedent.
4. Bonuses and on-costs corrected in the funds flow and treated as seller-borne.
5. Privacy incident investigated and assessed, with a specific uncapped indemnity and retention.

**Priority 2: Core SPA negotiation**
6. Remove general data room and public register disclosure (Sch. 7; DL §1.1–1.2).
7. Delete the buyer knowledge clause (cl. 8.3) and add an express pro-sandbagging clause.
8. Title and capacity outside the general cap, with a cap of at least the price and a long time limit.
9. Tax indemnity, outside cap and basket, with a statute-of-limitations time limit.
10. Carve fraud and non-excludable statutory rights out of the limitations and exclusive-remedy provisions.
11. Separate time limits for each class of claim, with general warranties at 24–36 months.

**Priority 3: Commercial terms**
12. General cap raised to at least 30–50% of price.
13. Tipping basket or smaller deductible; lower de minimis with related-claim aggregation.
14. Specific indemnities for Ironquay, the privacy incident and the Sandbar commitments.
15. Confirm lease, Mossvale and any other change-of-control consents, and obtain them where required.
16. Verify title independently (ASIC extract, register inspection, PPSR).
17. Bring-down disclosure and updated data room before signing.

**Overall position:** The Seller's package moves the known risks, roughly AUD 4.1m plus Bluefen revenue and the privacy exposure, onto the buyer while capping recovery at AUD 4.8m with a deductible, short time limits and a knowledge bar. It should not be accepted in its current form. The buyer should respond with a mark-up on the structure above and make the Priority 1 items conditions of signing or completion.

If useful, I can draft the mark-up language for any of these clauses, or a schedule of specific indemnities.
